problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-3,1),(1,-4),(1,0).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{90}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${90}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(-1,3)$
- $(4,1)$
- $(0,-1)$
worked_solution:
The counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{90}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${90}^{∘}$ is given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{{90}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}\,-3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \,\,\,-4 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{{90}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\,-3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \,\,\,-4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-1,-3),(4,1),(0,1).$

So, the correct answer is "II only."
